title: sticky-kv-cache-blocking-burst-reclamation-leads-to-reserved-pool-starvation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production customer escalations reported repeated dedicated pool capacity shortfalls during afternoon traffic spikes. Investigation shows long-lived KV cache sessions in the serving runtime prevented eviction of burst-eligible slots, causing reserved pool headroom to be depleted and blocking tenant burst reclamation. Several customers observed elevated 429/503 rates and increased latency despite available physical GPU capacity. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, hotfix deployment, verification, and long-term mitigations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy model variant with enabled persistent KV caching (runtime flag: kv.persistence=true) on dedicated pool
2) Start steady stream of chat requests that open long-running streaming connections and pin KV references (large context reuse),
3) Simulate burst traffic from a different tenant that should trigger burst reclamation and reserved pool allocation
4) Observe allocator metrics: freed_slots count does not increase, evictions are delayed, burst allocation fails — other tenants see 429s

root_cause: The allocator relies on reference counts of active KV handles to decide whether slots are reclaimable. A change in the serving runtime (kv:introduce-persistence) created session-scoped KV handles that were not cleared on request termination in edge cases (stream disconnects and partial chunk consumption). These stale references prevented the autoscaler from reclaiming slots, starving reserved pools of burstable capacity.
mitigation: Hotfix A: Add explicit eviction hint path when stream disconnects and garbage-collect session KV handles after idle timeout (hotfix applied)
Hotfix B: Temporary increase of reserved-pool headroom for impacted customers in region us-west-2
Operational: Added runbook steps to force-release stuck allocations via admin API (admin.reclaim_slots)
fix_details: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/9621 - add session-kv-timeout and on-disconnect eviction hook
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/481 - improve reclaimability check to ignore stale weak-refs older than 2m
Config change: default session_kv_ttl=120s applied behind flag 'kv.session-ttl'
Release note: runtime-1.22.3 contains the hotfix and admin reclaim tool updates
testing_and_release: Unit tests added for stream disconnect code paths and KV handle lifecycle
Integration: QA reproducer ran 50k requests with interleaved stream disconnects; no stuck allocations observed
Canary: Deployed to 5% of dedicated capacity on 2025-02-16, monitored for 48h
Full rollout: Gradual rollout completed on 2025-02-18 with rollback window and automated health gates
monitoring_and_next_steps: Dashboards: New metric 'stale_kv_refs' added to allocator dashboard (panel link below)
Alert: Pager rule created when stale_kv_refs > 50 for 5m in any region (alert ID: A-DED-KV-11)
Postmortem to be written by 2025-02-25; include code owners for allocator and serving-runtime
Follow-ups: (1) Audit other persistence flags for similar lifecycle gaps, (2) Add hard cap on session lifetime, (3) Add end-to-end chaos tests for stream disconnects
